candidates.entry: long the top 2 ETFs from [IEF, TLT, IEI] based on 60-day price momentum when momentum > 0
candidates.exit: exit when momentum falls below 0 or after 30-day hold period
candidates.sizing: equal weight across selected ETFs, targeting 10% annualized volatility
candidates.rationale: Inspired by cross-sectional bond momentum research, this strategy should capture excess returns from relative strength in intermediate and long-term Treasuries during stable market conditions.

candidates.entry: long TLT when estimated 10-year term premium (based on yield curve slope 10y-2y) is in top 20% of historical values over past 5 years
candidates.exit: exit when term premium drops below 50th percentile or after 60-day hold
candidates.sizing: fixed 100% allocation to TLT, scaled to 8% annualized volatility
candidates.rationale: Term premium predictability research suggests timing long-duration bonds like TLT during high premium periods can yield consistent excess returns outside recessions.

candidates.entry: long IEF and short SHY when the yield spread between intermediate and short-term Treasuries widens by more than 1 standard deviation over past 120 days
candidates.exit: exit when spread narrows to mean or after 45-day hold
candidates.sizing: dollar-neutral long-short position, targeting 6% annualized volatility
candidates.rationale: Liquidity premia in Treasuries, as per cited research, should provide a robust long-short return profile in low-rate environments.

candidates.entry: long TLT in low-volatility regime (identified by 20-day realized vol of TLT < 10%) and long SHY in high-volatility regime (> 10%)
candidates.exit: exit on regime switch or after 90-day hold
candidates.sizing: full allocation to selected ETF, scaled to 9% annualized volatility
candidates.rationale: Regime-switching models for duration exposure, as supported by research, should optimize risk-adjusted returns by adapting to volatility environments.

candidates.entry: long LQD when corporate credit spread (LQD yield minus IEF yield) is in top 25% of historical range over past 3 years
candidates.exit: exit when spread falls below 50th percentile or after 60-day hold
candidates.sizing: fixed 100% allocation to LQD, targeting 7% annualized volatility
candidates.regime_filter: skip when default risk premium (HYG yield minus LQD yield) > 5%
candidates.rationale: Credit spread term structure predictability, per cited research, should enable timing of investment-grade corporate bonds for excess returns in stable credit conditions.

notes_to_p3: For backtesting, ensure accurate yield curve data for term premium and spread calculations, ideally from yfinance or a reliable proxy like FRED integration. Regime filters involving VIX, NBER recessions, or volatility thresholds may require external data syncing. Transaction costs should be modeled conservatively for ETF trades (assume 2-5 bps per trade) given frequent rebalancing in some specs like momentum and regime-switching strategies. Watch for data gaps in early ETF history pre-2015 for some symbols like LQD or TLT.
